Package common.core.subsystems

Class MechanismBase

java.lang.Object
edu.wpi.first.wpilibj2.command.SubsystemBase
common.core.subsystems.MechanismBase
All Implemented Interfaces:
edu.wpi.first.util.sendable.Sendable, edu.wpi.first.wpilibj2.command.Subsystem
Direct Known Subclasses:
LinearMechanism, PivotMechanism, RollerMechanism
public abstract class MechanismBase extends edu.wpi.first.wpilibj2.command.SubsystemBase
What every mechanism has in common: one or more motors, driven to a setpoint, with logging, Shuffleboard tuning widgets and a safety timeout.

You'll usually use one of its subclasses instead of this class itself: LinearMechanism for elevators and sliders, PivotMechanism for arms, wrists, hoods and turrets, and RollerMechanism for intakes and flywheels.

Using a mechanism

  • setSetpoint(double) moves it to a position or speed, in its own units (set by MotorConfig), and keeps it there.
  • run(double) and runVolts(double) drive it directly, without a setpoint.
  • stop() stops it; reset() tells it it's at its starting position, e.g. when it's against a hard stop.

Where the control loop runs

A control loop measures the mechanism, compares it with the setpoint, and works out the volts to send (see PIDFFConfig for the gains). It can run in one of two places:
  • On the motor controller, the usual choice. The TalonFX or Spark runs PID and feedforward 1000 times a second on its own encoder, 50 times faster than robot code runs. Gains are given in the mechanism's units and converted for the motor controller. 
    super(gains, Control.Position, TOLERANCE, HOME, MOTOR_CONFIG, motor);
  • On the roboRIO, for a WPILib controller like a BangBangController, or when the measurement doesn't come from the motor's encoder, e.g. a gyro or camera. The controller works out volts from (measurement, setpoint): 
    super(gains, pid::calculate, m -> pid.reset(), gyro::getAngle, TOLERANCE, HOME, MOTOR_CONFIG, motor);

Anything the motor controller can't work out itself, like gravity on a wrist that depends on the arm it's on, goes in calculateFeedforward(double), which runs on the roboRIO and is sent along with each setpoint.

Several motors

When several motors drive one mechanism, the first is the leader and the rest follow it on the motor controller where possible. Only the leader runs the control loop.

Logging and 3D

Every loop, the setpoint, measurement, volts, and each motor's current and temperature are logged under Mechanisms/<name> in NetworkTables, for AdvantageScope. getComponentPose() gives where its moving part is for AdvantageScope's 3D view, and setParent(MechanismBase) mounts it on another mechanism, e.g. a wrist on an arm.

  • Constructor Details

    • MechanismBase

      public MechanismBase(PIDFFConfig gains, NAR_Motor.Control controllerMode, double tolerance, double resetPosition, NAR_Motor.MotorConfig motorConfig, NAR_Motor... motors)
      Creates a mechanism whose PID runs on the leader's motor controller.
      Parameters:
      gains - kP/kI/kD in volts per unit of error, kS and kG in volts, kV in volts per unit of velocity; converted for the motor controller.
      controllerMode - NAR_Motor.Control.Position or NAR_Motor.Control.Velocity.
      tolerance - Error tolerance for atSetpoint().
      resetPosition - Position the motors are reset to by reset(), e.g. the mechanism's home position.
      motorConfig - Hardware configuration applied to every motor; sets the units.
      motors - The motor(s) driven by this mechanism. The first is the leader.

    • MechanismBase

      public MechanismBase(PIDFFConfig gains, DoubleBinaryOperator feedback, DoubleConsumer resetController, DoubleSupplier measurement, double tolerance, double resetPosition, NAR_Motor.MotorConfig motorConfig, NAR_Motor... motors)
      Creates a mechanism whose control loop runs on the roboRIO.
      Parameters:
      gains - Feedforward gains; also handed to calculateFeedforward(double).
      feedback - The WPILib controller's calculate(measurement, setpoint) method reference.
      resetController - Resets the controller's internal state (integral, previous error, profile) given the current measurement; called when the mechanism goes from disabled to enabled. Use m -> pid.reset() for a PIDController, profiled::reset for a ProfiledPIDController, or m -> {} for a BangBangController.
      measurement - Supplies the mechanism's current measurement, e.g. leader::getPosition.
      tolerance - Error tolerance for atSetpoint().
      resetPosition - Position the motors are reset to by reset(), e.g. the mechanism's home position.
      motorConfig - Hardware configuration applied to every motor.
      motors - The motor(s) driven by this mechanism. The first is the leader.

    • MechanismBase

      protected MechanismBase(PIDFFConfig gains, NAR_Motor.Control controllerMode, DoubleBinaryOperator feedback, DoubleConsumer resetController, DoubleSupplier measurement, double tolerance, double resetPosition, NAR_Motor.MotorConfig motorConfig, NAR_Motor... motors)

    • MechanismBase

      public MechanismBase(NAR_Motor.MotorConfig motorConfig, NAR_Motor... motors)
      Creates an open-loop-only mechanism, with no PID/feedforward loop. enable()/setSetpoint(double) are unavailable; use run(double) or runVolts(double) directly. The measurement defaults to the first motor's position so Shuffleboard widgets still work.

  • Method Details

    • applyGains

      public void applyGains()
      Sends the PID and feedforward gains to the motor controllers. Call again after changing gains, e.g. from Shuffleboard. Does nothing when the roboRIO runs the loop.

    • useArmGravity

      protected void useArmGravity(double motorRotationsPerArmRotation)
      Makes the motor controller multiply kG by the cosine of the arm's angle instead of applying it as a constant. Position 0 must be the arm held horizontal.
      Parameters:
      motorRotationsPerArmRotation - Rotations of the leader's encoder per arm rotation: the gearing, or 1 for an absolute encoder on the arm's shaft

    • useRoboRioGravity

      protected void useRoboRioGravity()
      Leaves kG out of what the motor controller applies, for when gravity depends on something it can't measure, e.g. a wrist's on the arm it's mounted on. Work kG out in calculateFeedforward(double) instead; it's sent with each setpoint.

    • invertMotor

      public void invertMotor(int motorIndex)
      Makes one motor spin the opposite way to motorConfig, e.g. when it faces the other way.

    • setStatorLimit

      public void setStatorLimit(int amps)
      Sets the stator current limit of every motor, e.g. to push gently against a hard stop.

    • calculateFeedforward

      protected double calculateFeedforward(double pidOutput)
      Feedforward worked out on the roboRIO, in volts. Default is none.

      When the roboRIO runs the loop, override this to add e.g. gains.positionFF(pidOutput, atSetpoint()). When the motor controller runs the loop it already applies kS, kV and kG, so only override this for anything extra it can't do, e.g. a kG that changes with an elevator's height.

      Parameters:
      pidOutput - The output of feedback this cycle, or the error (setpoint minus measurement) when the motor controller runs the loop. Use it to sign kS.

    • periodic

      public void periodic()
      Runs every robot loop (50 times a second). While a setpoint is active, it sends the setpoint to the motors, checks the safety timeout, and stops if it should once there. It always logs.

    • getMotorConfig

      public NAR_Motor.MotorConfig getMotorConfig()
      The hardware settings every motor got: gearing, current limit, inversion and brake mode.

    • setSafetyThresh

      public void setSafetyThresh(double timeSeconds)
      Sets how long it can go without being at its setpoint before it gives up and stops, e.g. because it's jammed. The clock restarts every time it reaches the setpoint.
      Parameters:
      timeSeconds - How long, in seconds; 5 by default

    • onSafetyTimeout

      public void onSafetyTimeout()
      Called when the safety timeout runs out. Logs a warning and stops the motors. Override it to do something else.

    • setSetpoint

      public void setSetpoint(double setpoint)
      Moves to setpoint and keeps the control loop running. It's limited to the range from setInputRange(double, double). While the Shuffleboard DEBUG switch is on, the Debug_Setpoint box is used instead.
      Parameters:
      setpoint - A position or speed, in this mechanism's units

    • setSetpointCommand

      public edu.wpi.first.wpilibj2.command.Command setSetpointCommand(double setpoint)
      A command that calls setSetpoint(double) and finishes right away, without waiting to get there. Follow it with waitUntil(mechanism::atSetpoint) to wait.

    • setDisableAtSetpoint

      public void setDisableAtSetpoint(boolean disableAtSetpoint)
      Sets whether it stops once atSetpoint() is true. Defaults to true, which suits a roller; set it to false for mechanisms that must keep holding, e.g. an elevator.

    • setInputRange

      public void setInputRange(double min, double max)
      Limits every setpoint passed to setSetpoint(double) to [min, max]. Unlimited by default.

      The last setpoint, after limiting it to the input range.

    • atSetpoint

      Whether the measurement is within the tolerance of the setpoint.

    • enable

      public void enable()
      Starts the control loop, without changing the setpoint. setSetpoint(double) calls this for you. A roboRIO controller is reset first if the loop wasn't already running, so it doesn't start with old leftovers like a built-up kI.

    • disable

      public void disable()
      Stops the control loop. If it was running, the motors stop too, so they don't keep their last output.

    • isEnabled

      public boolean isEnabled()
      Whether the control loop is running.

    • run

      public void run(double power)
      Drives the motors at a fraction of full power, stopping the control loop.
      Parameters:
      power - From -1 (full reverse) to 1 (full forward)

    • runCommand

      public edu.wpi.first.wpilibj2.command.Command runCommand(double power)

    • runVolts

      public void runVolts(double volts)
      Drives the motors at a voltage, stopping the control loop. Unlike run(double), the motor gets the same push however charged the battery is.

    • characterization

      public edu.wpi.first.wpilibj2.command.Command characterization(double rampRate, double stepVoltage)
      A SysId routine that drives the mechanism with rising and stepped voltages and records how it responds, so WPILib's SysId tool can work out its kS, kV, kA and kG. Each of its four tests runs for up to 10 seconds, so give it room to move, and cancel it before it hits a hard stop.
      Parameters:
      rampRate - Volts per second for the slowly rising test
      stepVoltage - Volts for the sudden-step test

    • addControllerWidget

      protected void addControllerWidget(edu.wpi.first.util.sendable.Sendable controller, int x, int y, int width, int height)
      Adds the underlying WPILib controller's own Shuffleboard widget (it already implements Sendable), e.g. addControllerWidget(pid).

    • initShuffleboard

      public void initShuffleboard()
      Adds a Shuffleboard tab for tuning: the setpoint and measurement with graphs, boxes to type the feedforward gains, and buttons to run it. Turn on the DEBUG switch to use the buttons and the Debug_Setpoint box; while it's on, the box overrides every setpoint.
